beats.lead: Instagram wasn't built as a photo app
beats.text: It started as a location check-in app called Burbn.
beats.note: Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger built it in San Francisco to compete with Foursquare — check-ins, plans with friends, points for going out. Photos were just one feature, buried among many.

beats.context: How many people Burbn had after three months. By most measures, it was already failing.

beats.lead: So they looked at what people actually used it for
beats.text: Almost nobody cared about check-ins. Everyone shared photos.
beats.note: Systrom and Krieger stripped out everything else and rebuilt the whole app around the one feature people kept coming back for.

beats.lead: One thing still stood in the way
beats.text: People didn't think their photos looked good enough to post.
beats.note: Kevin's wife told him that was the real reason people hesitated. His answer became Instagram's first filter, X-Pro II.

beats.text: The app launched as Instagram on 6 October 2010. Two months later it had a million users — the same idea that, as Burbn, had never broken a hundred.

beats.line: A failed check-in app, one feature away from Instagram.
